- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast peaks at +10% above prior high or use lagged mean to dampen momentum.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 2–3% buffer to forecast for bullish sentiment.  
- Model consistently underpredicts late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment for final 7–10 days if sentiment is positive.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; use 3-day moving average of true values to anchor forecast mid-range.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 10-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish; use sentiment as trigger for floor protection.
